acceptance: Either (a) every Phase 2 vectorized Python generator met its ADR budget and this gate is closed via finish with a closing_note recording the measured budgets (no Rust repository created), OR (b) owner approved creating BenchBox-dev/benchbox-datagen for named budget-missing benchmark(s).

If created: repository contains only one library crate and one binary crate, ships binary-only Maturin wheels (py3-none-<platform>, CLI-only, no PyO3/ABI tracking), and designs its generator trait strictly from the first failing generator's needs.

If created: CI verifies identical golden per-table hashes across thread counts (1 vs default) and across every released OS/architecture (pinned rand/rand_chacha with owned sampling, pure-Rust libm or integer math for transcendentals, fixed-block RNG state).

If created: binary prints JSON per-file stats (Python DataGenerationManifest stays the sole manifest writer), schema-sync against schema.py runs in benchbox CI with zero circular dependency, and benchbox integrates it strictly as an optional extra pinned in uv.lock.

description:
## Problem
Creating and maintaining a second-language Rust repository (BenchBox-dev/benchbox-datagen) adds build, release-matrix, and cross-platform determinism cost for a single maintainer. Per docs/internal/adr/adr-python-core-runtime.md and owner decision A1, the repository must only be created if a synthetic generator still misses its Phase 0 ADR wall-time or peak-RSS budget after Python vectorization.

## Change
- Evaluate a recorded Linux SF 10 converter budget miss from datagen-p1-deterministic-parquet-writer, if any.
- Evaluate Gate D measurements from datagen-p2-vectorize-synthetic-generators (and any SSB budget miss if datagen-p2-ssb-versioned-migration has already completed).
- If every synthetic benchmark meets its ADR budget in vectorized Python: create NO repository and close this item via finish with a closing_note summarizing the measured budgets (do not drop, so datagen-p3-synthetic-cutover unlocks cleanly).
- Only if one or more benchmarks still miss budget after vectorization AND owner explicitly approves:
  1. Bootstrap BenchBox-dev/benchbox-datagen with minimal structure: one library crate + one binary crate (no speculative multi-crate workspace or specs/ mirror).
  2. Package as a binary-only Maturin wheel (py3-none-<platform>, CLI-only, no PyO3 module or Python ABI matrix) covering every supported BenchBox platform for the target benchmark (or explicitly retaining legacy on uncovered platforms).
  3. Design the generator trait directly from the first approved failing generator's needs.
  4. Enforce cross-platform bit-exact determinism: per-(benchmark, table, seed, block_index) RNG with fixed block size, pinned rand/rand_chacha + owned sampling code, pure-Rust libm or integer arithmetic for sin/ln/powf, streaming atomic I/O with _generation_in_progress, and JSON per-file stats output.
  5. Wire into benchbox behind --datagen-backend native as an optional extra pinned in uv.lock, running schema-sync (schema.py) and Gate A/C/D checks in benchbox CI (zero dependency from the Rust repo on benchbox).

## Decision gates
- Hard stop before creating any new repository: requires a recorded Phase 2 Gate D budget miss AND explicit owner approval.
- If all benchmarks met budget in Phase 2, close with finish (not drop) so downstream Phase 3 unlocks automatically.

## Guardrails
- Never add a second _datagen_manifest.json writer in Rust; Python DataGenerationManifest remains the sole emitter.
- Never introduce a circular dependency from BenchBox-dev/benchbox-datagen to BenchBox-dev/BenchBox.
- Never promote benchbox-datagen to a required dependency of core benchbox (core stays py3-none-any).
- If SSB later misses budget after datagen-p2-ssb-versioned-migration runs, either add it to an existing BenchBox-dev/benchbox-datagen repo or open a targeted follow-up item gated by the same criteria.
